cityQuote: Whoever lies awake at night in Sarajevo hears the voices of the Sarajevo night.
cityQuoteAttribution: Ivo Andrić, “A Letter from 1920,” on hearing the city’s cathedral, Orthodox church, and mosques mark the hours
heroTitle: Sarajevo hero — Julian Nyča (CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons)
wordsPreamble:
- Sarajevo speaks Bosnian. It is close enough to Serbian and Croatian that speakers of all three understand each other easily.
- It is written in the Latin alphabet. Č and ć are both “ch,” š is “sh,” ž is “zh,” c is “ts,” and j is “y.”
- Many Bosniaks greet each other with “merhaba” or “selam,” from Turkish and Arabic.
- The currency is the convertible mark (KM). Euros are often accepted, at about two marks to the euro.
